## 2. How the accessory is installed

It is an **`NSTitlebarAccessoryViewController` hosting SwiftUI**, not an `NSToolbar`.

- `RootView.swift:412`: `.background(TitlebarAccessoryHost { accessoryBarContent })` on the whole window-chrome content.
- `TitlebarAccessoryHost.swift` (`NSViewRepresentable`): `Coordinator.install(on:)` (`48-71`) creates `NSTitlebarAccessoryViewController()`, sets `vc.layoutAttribute = .left` (`54`), `vc.view = hosting.view` (an `NSHostingController<AnyView>`, `55`), then `window.addTitlebarAccessoryViewController(vc)` (`56`). Guarded by an `installed` flag so it's added exactly once per window.
- **Frame/height** — a `.left` accessory doesn't auto-fill, so `updateFrame()` (`82-93`) sets it explicitly: width = `max(window.frame.width - WorkroomTitlebar.trafficLightInset(80), 120)`; height = `window.standardWindowButton(.closeButton)?.superview?.frame.height ?? WorkroomTitlebar.height(28)` — i.e. it tracks the *actual* traffic-light container height (the taller `.unified` toolbar row), not the 28pt constant. Re-measured on `NSWindow.didResizeNotification` and `didUpdateNotification` (`64-69`); write is idempotent (`92`).
- **Transparency**: `applyTransparency()` (`77-80`) sets `hosting.view.wantsLayer/backgroundColor = .clear`, re-applied on every SwiftUI update (`updateNSView`, `33`) because `NSHostingController` resets to opaque on re-render.
- Companion AppKit window setup lives in `Core/WindowBackgroundThemer.swift`: `window.styleMask.insert(.fullSizeContentView)` (`41`), `window.titlebarAppearsTransparent = true` (`42`), `window.titleVisibility = .hidden` (`48`), **`window.toolbar?.isVisible = false`** (`63`) — an actual `NSToolbar` exists only so SwiftUI's `.unified` toolbar-style machinery grows the title-bar row/centers the traffic lights, and it's then hidden outright (comment `43-62` explains this avoids `NavigationSplitView`'s auto-injected sidebar-toggle toolbar item, which otherwise renders a stray "»" overflow and drives a macOS-26 AppHang), `window.titlebarSeparatorStyle = .none` (`65`), `window.backgroundColor = theme.nsPanel` (`69`).
- `WorkroomTitlebar` constants (`TitlebarBars.swift:9-16`): `height = 28`, `trafficLightInset = 80`.
- Note: `TitlebarBars.swift`'s file-level doc comment (`4-8`) and the dead `RootView.titlebarBar` var describe an earlier "draw as full-size-content top strip" approach; the code that actually runs today is the `.left` `NSTitlebarAccessoryViewController` path in `TitlebarAccessoryHost`/`RootView.swift:412`.

## 3. Run command buttons

Defined in `TargetDetailToolbar.swift:72-112` (`RunControls`), instantiated from `TrailingTitlebarBar` (`TitlebarBars.swift:164-166`) with `target = store.selectedTarget` and `projectPath = AppStore.projectPath(of: store.selectedTargetID)`. All state lives in `AppStore.swift`:
- Gate: `canRunCommand(for:inProject:)` (`1151-1153`) = `!target.isMissing && hasRunCommand(forProject:)`.
- `hasRunCommand(forProject:)` (`1144-1146`) → `runConfig(forProject:)` (`1139-1142`) reads `Defaults[.runCommands][projectPath]` — a **per-project** `RunConfig{command, autoRun}` (`Core/DefaultsKeys.swift:8-16`), configured via `ProjectSettingsSheet.swift` → `AppStore.setRunConfig` (`1158-1169`). Per the struct's doc comment (`DefaultsKeys.swift:3-4`): configured per **project** but executed in the **selected workroom's** directory.
- `isRunCommandRunning(for:)` (`1129-1131`) reads `runStates[targetID]?.isRunning`.
- `runOrFocusRunCommand()` (`1630-1670`) — the Run-button action: a state machine over `runStates[target.id]` (`.running`/`.restarting`/`.stopped`/`.armed`/`.none`), including single-owner-across-windows via `WindowRegistry.runOwner` and (issue #127) opening `ProjectSettingsSheet` with a warning when no command is configured.
- `stopRunCommand(for:)` (`1711-1719`) sends `SIGUSR2` to the run supervisor; `restartRunCommand(for:)` (`1726-1737`) sends `SIGUSR1` or respawns if the supervisor is gone.

## 4. "Open in…" button

Defined in `TargetDetailToolbar.swift:9-65` (`OpenInControl`), instantiated from `TrailingTitlebarBar` (`TitlebarBars.swift:163`) with `path = target.path`.
- Editor list: `ExternalEditor.installed` (`Core/ExternalEditor.swift:19-26`) filters the hardcoded `supported` table (`12-16`: VS Code `com.microsoft.VSCode`, Zed `dev.zed.Zed`, Xcode `com.apple.dt.Xcode`) down to what `NSWorkspace.shared.urlForApplication(withBundleIdentifier:)` resolves.
- State: `@Default(.lastEditor)` (`"openInEditorBundleID"`, `DefaultsKeys.swift:52`) — the primary icon click always opens the last-picked editor (`remembered`, computed at `TargetDetailToolbar.swift:18`); the chevron `Menu` lists every installed editor and picking one both updates `lastEditorID` and opens immediately (`ExternalEditor.open`, `ExternalEditor.swift:54-60`, calls `NSWorkspace.shared.open(withApplicationAt:)`).
- Renders nothing when `editors.isEmpty` (`TargetDetailToolbar.swift:17,63`).
- Gap: neither the icon button nor the chevron menu carries an `accessibilityIdentifier` — only dynamic `.accessibilityLabel`s (`"Open in \(remembered.name)"`, `"Choose editor"`) — unlike `RunControls`' stable ids.

## 5. Keyboard-shortcut / menu duplicates and UITest identifiers

- **Sidebar toggle** — Menu: `WorkroomCommands` "Projects" `Toggle`, `CommandGroup(replacing: .sidebar)`, `⌃⌘S` (`WorkroomApp.swift:801-805`). AppDelegate key monitor additionally traps `⌃⌘S` (`318-323`), `⌥⌘S` (`324-337`, overriding AppKit's native `toggleSidebar:`), and `⌥⌘B` (`338-343`) — three combos, one `store.sidebarVisible.toggle()`. Id `"toolbar.toggleSidebar"` — no UITest reference found.
- **Back/Forward** — Go-menu `"Back"`/`"Forward"`, `⌘[`/`⌘]` (`WorkroomApp.swift:1070-1075`), same `store.navigateBack/Forward`. No identifiers on the buttons.
- **Run/Stop/Restart** — Run menu `CommandMenu("Run")` (`939-949`, `⌘R`/`⌥⌘R`/`⇧⌘R`) *and* the `AppDelegate` key monitor traps the same three combos directly (`267-288`, calling `runOrFocusRunCommand`/`stopSelectedRunCommand`/`restartSelectedRunCommand` on `store.selectedTarget`, before menu or terminal see them). Ids `"runCommand.run"`/`.stop`/`.restart` (`TargetDetailToolbar.swift:88,97,108`) **are** exercised: `WorkroomAppUITests/RunStatusUITests.swift:33,67`, `WorkroomWorkflowUITests.swift:143-158`, `TerminalAgentUITests.swift:31`.
- **Open in…** — Go-menu `"Open in \(editor)"`, `⇧⌘O` (`WorkroomApp.swift:1082-1086`), same `store.openSelectedInEditor()` (`AppStore.swift:766-770`, gated by `canOpenInEditor` at `758-761`). No accessibility identifier and **no UITest coverage found** (grep for "Open in"/"OpenIn"/"openIn" across `WorkroomAppUITests` is empty).
- **Quick Terminal** — File-menu `"Quick Terminal"` item, same `⌥§` and same notification post (`WorkroomApp.swift:1018-1024`); plus a global Carbon `⌥§` hotkey in non-Debug builds that calls `quickTerminal.toggle()` directly, bypassing the notification (`updateGlobalHotkey`, `409-417`). Id `"toolbar.quickTerminal"` — no UITest reference found.
- **Update pill** — App-menu `"Check for Updates…"` (`WorkroomApp.swift:766-767`), same `updater.checkForUpdates()`. Id `"toolbar.update"` — no UITest reference found.
- **New/Open workroom (+ / ⌄)** — File-menu `"New Workroom…"` `⌘N` / `"Open Workroom…"` `⌘O` (`WorkroomApp.swift:984-995`). Ids `"NewWorkroom"`/`"OpenWorkroom"` **are** exercised: `TabStripOverflowUITests.swift:187,202,212`, `TabStripScrollIntoViewUITests.swift:191`.

10	/// Workroom-into-workroom split renderer (issue #23 follow-up): renders `PaneLayout<SidebarID>` as
11	/// nested, resizable panes — each a full `TargetTerminalDetail`. Deliberately SEPARATE from the
12	/// terminal renderer `PaneTreeView` (whose re-parenting/blank-pane history makes surgery risky); it
13	/// reuses only the pure `PaneTreeLayout` geometry + the generic `PaneLayout` model and duplicates a
14	/// little view chrome (divider, focus border, drop band).
15	///
16	/// Like `PaneTreeView`, panes are laid out in ONE flat `ZStack`, positioned by absolute frames and
17	/// keyed by `SidebarID`, so a surviving pane keeps the exact same host across a layout change (only its
18	/// frame moves) — its terminal is never re-parented. `RootView` ALWAYS renders through this view when
19	/// the tab bar is on (a no-split case is just `.leaf(selected)`), so single↔split is a leaf-set change,
20	/// not a structural swap — the same lesson that made `WorkroomTerminalsView` always render through
21	/// `PaneTreeView`.
22	struct WorkroomSplitView: View {
23	  /// The app store, threaded to each leaf as a plain (non-observed) reference so the workroom
24	  /// context menu (issue #112) can read/mutate it WITHOUT subscribing this terminal-hosting view
25	  /// tree to the whole churny store. NOT `@EnvironmentObject`/`@ObservedObject` on purpose.
26	  let store: AppStore
27	  let layout: PaneLayout<SidebarID>
28	  /// Resolve a leaf to its live target (drops a since-deleted workroom). Owned by the store.
29	  let resolve: (SidebarID) -> TerminalTarget?
30	  let focusedID: SidebarID?
31	  /// The live drag of a workroom into the content — from the tab bar OR a split member's group title
32	  /// bar (issue #110). Drives the drop-edge highlight; a member's title bar writes it while dragging.
33	  @Binding var externalDrag: WorkroomPaneDrag?
34	  /// Content-local point for a global drag location (nil when over the title-bar strip). Owned by
35	  /// `RootView`; shared with the tab bar so a title-bar drag drops onto the same panes a chip would.
36	  let localize: (CGPoint) -> CGPoint?
37	  /// Where a drag at a global location lands (member pane + edge), or nil if not over a pane.
38	  let dropTarget: (CGPoint) -> (sid: SidebarID, edge: PaneEdge)?
39	  let onFocus: (SidebarID) -> Void
40	  let onSetRatio: (CGFloat, UUID) -> Void
41	  let onClose: (SidebarID) -> Void
42	  /// Move a member to land beside another at an edge (drag a group by its title bar). Wired to
43	  /// `store.insertWorkroomSplit`, the same transform the tab-bar chip drop uses.
44	  let onMove: (SidebarID, SidebarID, PaneEdge) -> Void
45	
46	  private static let space = "workroomSplitContent"
47	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
48	
49	  var body: some View {
50	    let leaves = layout.tabIDs
51	    let multi = leaves.count >= 2
52	    GeometryReader { geo in
53	      let plan = PaneTreeLayout.plan(layout, in: CGRect(origin: .zero, size: geo.size))
54	      ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) {
55	        ForEach(leaves, id: \.self) { sid in
56	          if let target = resolve(sid), let rect = plan.panes[sid] {
57	            WorkroomPaneLeaf(
58	              store: store, sid: sid, target: target, focused: sid == focusedID, multi: multi,
59	              externalDrag: $externalDrag, localize: localize, dropTarget: dropTarget,
60	              onClose: { onClose(sid) }, onMove: onMove
61	            )
62	            .frame(width: rect.width, height: rect.height)
63	            .position(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
64	            .id(sid)
65	            // A tap on the pane *chrome* focuses it. Clicking *into* the terminal is handled by the
66	            // first-responder → selection callback (the libghostty NSView eats SwiftUI taps).
67	            .onTapGesture { onFocus(sid) }
68	          }
69	        }
70	        ForEach(plan.dividers) { d in
71	          WorkroomSplitDivider(orientation: d.orientation, ratio: d.ratio, total: d.total) {
72	            onSetRatio($0, d.id)
73	          }
74	          .frame(width: d.hitRect.width, height: d.hitRect.height)
75	          .position(x: d.rect.midX, y: d.rect.midY)
76	        }
77	        dropHighlight(plan: plan)
78	      }
79	      .coordinateSpace(.named(Self.space))
80	    }
81	    // When split, hold the group cards off the left/right sidebars with an outer gutter (issue #110) —
82	    // applied outside the GeometryReader so the panes reflow within the inset. Solo is flush as before.
83	    .padding(.horizontal, multi ? 6 : 0)
84	  }

86	  /// The accent band previewing where a dragged workroom tab will land (mirrors `PaneTreeView`).
87	  @ViewBuilder
88	  private func dropHighlight(plan: PaneTreeLayout.Plan<SidebarID>) -> some View {
89	    if let drag = externalDrag,
90	      let hit = PaneTreeLayout.dropTarget(at: drag.location, panes: plan.panes),
91	      hit.tab != drag.sid, let rect = plan.panes[hit.tab]
92	    {
93	      let band = PaneTreeLayout.edgeBand(hit.edge, in: rect)
94	      RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)
95	        .fill(theme.tokens.accent.opacity(0.25))
96	        .overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).strokeBorder(theme.tokens.accent, lineWidth: 2))
97	        .frame(width: band.width, height: band.height)
98	        .position(x: band.midX, y: band.midY)
99	        .allowsHitTesting(false)
100	        .transition(.opacity)
101	    }
102	  }

319	/// A draggable divider that writes a new ratio for one split node. A near-twin of `PaneTreeView`'s
320	/// private `SplitDivider` (kept separate so the terminal renderer stays untouched), reusing the shared
321	/// `PaneTreeLayout.clampRatio`/`dividerThickness` math. Unlike `SplitDivider` it draws **no** separator
322	/// rule — each workroom pane already has its own rounded border, so a line in the gap would double up;
323	/// this is just the (invisible) resize hit-zone, surfaced only by the resize cursor on hover.
324	private struct WorkroomSplitDivider: View {
325	  let orientation: SplitOrientation
326	  let ratio: CGFloat
327	  let total: CGFloat
328	  let onRatio: (CGFloat) -> Void
329	  @State private var startRatio: CGFloat?
330	
331	  var body: some View {
332	    Rectangle()
333	      .fill(Color.secondary.opacity(0.0001))
334	      .contentShape(Rectangle())
335	      .gesture(
336	        DragGesture(coordinateSpace: .global)
337	          .onChanged { value in
338	            let start = startRatio ?? ratio
339	            if startRatio == nil { startRatio = start }
340	            let usable = max(1, total - PaneTreeLayout.dividerThickness)
341	            let delta =
342	              orientation == .horizontal ? value.translation.width : value.translation.height
343	            onRatio(
344	              PaneTreeLayout.clampRatio(start + delta / usable, total: total, along: orientation))
345	          }
346	          .onEnded { _ in startRatio = nil }
347	      )
348	      .onHover { inside in
349	        if inside {
350	          (orientation == .horizontal ? NSCursor.resizeLeftRight : NSCursor.resizeUpDown).push()
351	        } else {
352	          NSCursor.pop()
353	        }
354	      }
355	      .accessibilityElement()
356	      .accessibilityIdentifier("workroom.pane.divider")
357	      .accessibilityLabel(
358	        orientation == .horizontal ? "Vertical workroom divider" : "Horizontal workroom divider"
359	      )
360	      .accessibilityValue("\(Int((ratio * 100).rounded()))%")
361	      .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
362	        let step: CGFloat = 0.05
363	        switch direction {
364	        case .increment:
365	          onRatio(PaneTreeLayout.clampRatio(ratio + step, total: total, along: orientation))
366	        case .decrement:
367	          onRatio(PaneTreeLayout.clampRatio(ratio - step, total: total, along: orientation))
368	        @unknown default: break
369	        }
370	      }
371	  }
372	}

# macapp/CLAUDE.md

The Workroom macOS app: a SwiftUI (macOS 15+) front-end that bundles the `workroom`
Go binary and drives it over the CLI's `--json` contract. See README.md for full
architecture, signing, and notarization detail — this file is the quick reference.

## Dev tasks (Makefile)

Every dev task runs through the **repo-root `Makefile`**, namespaced `app-*` (run from the repo
root, not `macapp/`):

```bash
make app-run        # canonical local loop: xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug) → relaunch
make app-build      # xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug)
make app-test       # xcodebuild test (WorkroomAppTests) — parallel; APP_TEST_FLAGS= to serialize
make app-generate   # force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
make app-vcs        # build the Rust VCS core → WrVcs SwiftPM package (auto-run before app builds)
make app-format     # swift-format, rewrite sources in place
make app-lint       # swift-format --strict (non-zero on any violation — the hard gate)
make app-release    # Release build → notarize → staple → DMG installer (Scripts/release.sh)
make app-icon       # regenerate AppIcon PNGs (Scripts/make-icon.swift)
make app-clean      # remove DerivedData + .xcodeproj
```

Builds reuse `macapp/DerivedData/` so the Swift packages (incl. the GhosttyKit xcframework)
aren't re-resolved/re-downloaded every build. (`cli-*` targets cover the Go CLI — see the root
CLAUDE.md.)

## VCS core (Rust jj + SwiftGitX git)

Workroom reads VCS data through **two backends behind one Swift layer** (the app is growing into a
VCS-first IDE — issue #59 is the first brick):

- **jj → Rust `jj-lib` via UniFFI.** The `vcs/` Rust workspace (jj-only) builds a static xcframework
  + generated Swift into the local SwiftPM package `vcs/swift/WrVcs` — the app does `import WrVcs`.
- **git → SwiftGitX (libgit2), pure Swift.** git has a mature native Swift path; jj has none — so
  only jj needs the Rust/UniFFI bridge. (An all-Rust core with gix was tried and dropped: gix bought
  no real unification and libgit2 is the more complete git engine.)

**Three reads reach past SwiftGitX**, all linking the `libgit2` C API **directly** (its own SPM package
in `project.yml`, URL + version identical to SwiftGitX's own dependency so SwiftPM sees one package
identity). `Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init` and hands out raw `git_repository`
handles (SwiftGitX inits inside `Repository.open`, which a direct C caller can't rely on); these four
files are the only ones in the app touching raw libgit2:

- **Push state — `Core/GitGraph.swift`.** SwiftGitX cannot express a commit *range*: its
  `CommitSequence` only calls `git_revwalk_push`, never `git_revwalk_hide`, it exposes no
  merge-base/graph helper, and its repository pointer is `internal` — so "which commits aren't on
  `origin` yet" (`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*`) needs the C API. The jj side answers the same
  question natively with one `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)` revset. Push state is
  **origin-scoped** and any unreadable ref degrades the WHOLE page to "unknown" (no badge) rather than
  a partial answer.
- **Commit diffs — `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`.** Rename detection is `git_diff_find_similar` run over a
  live `git_diff`, and a SwiftGitX `Diff` materializes its deltas/patches in an `internal` init and
  frees the `git_diff` before returning, so there's nothing left to detect on. Without it a committed
  rename read as delete + add while `git show` showed one rename row (git defaults to
  `diff.renames=true`), and a root commit's diff came back empty (SwiftGitX diffs it against itself).
  Detection options are NULL, which is what makes libgit2 read the repo's own `diff.renames` /
  `diff.renamelimit` — naming a flag explicitly suppresses that config read, so a repo set to
  `diff.renames=false` or `=copies` would silently disagree with its own CLI. Typechanges are included
  (`GIT_DIFF_INCLUDE_TYPECHANGE`); without it libgit2 splits a file↔symlink change into delete + add
  on the SAME path, giving the file list two rows with one `id`. `GitProvider.changeset`/`.fileDiff`
  both read through it, so the History file list and the patch text can't disagree.
- **Working-tree ± line counts — `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`**, via `git_diff_get_stats`. SwiftGitX
  surfaces no diffstat, and its `Diff` is **eager**: `Diff.init` builds a `Patch` per delta and
  materializes every hunk line into a Swift `String` before the caller sees it. Summing those for the
  badge cost one `String` per changed line of the whole worktree on **every** status refresh, so the
  counts moved to libgit2, which counts in C and allocates nothing Swift-side. The diff itself is
  irreducible — that's what `git diff --shortstat` costs too. With `changeset` now counting through
  `GitCommitDiff`, **no** `+N −M` in the app is summed off SwiftGitX hunk lines any more, which also
  ends a real bug: that sum counted the EOFNL markers (`\ No newline at end of file`) as lines, so
  changing only a file's trailing newline reported two deletions where git reports `1 insertion(+),
  1 deletion(-)`. libgit2 skips them, as `git diff --shortstat`/`--numstat` do. It runs
  `git_diff_find_similar` too, for the same reason `GitCommitDiff` does: the file list beside these
  counts already pairs renames (libgit2 status' `.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so without it
  a staged rename rendered as one "renamed" row badged `+N −N` while `git diff HEAD --shortstat`
  reported `0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

**Read surface & routing.** `Core/VCSProviding.swift` is the one Swift protocol; `VCS.provider(for:)`
routes by repo kind. `RustJJProvider` maps `WrVcs.*` → app-native models, `GitProvider` wraps
SwiftGitX. `WorkroomStatusResolver` and `BranchResolver` read through this layer — **the jj CLI
parsers are gone** (log/changeset/currentRef/workingStatus are all native jj-lib).

**The one mutating read: `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`.** jj's working copy is itself a commit, so
on-disk edits don't exist to jj-lib until snapshotted — a working-copy status read therefore *must*
snapshot `@` first: it takes the working-copy lock and rewrites `@` (modeled on jayjay's
`refresh_working_copy`). Everything else (log/changeset/currentRef) is a read-only `load_at_head`
with no lock. Because it mutates, **only test snapshot changes on throwaway repos** (corruption
risk). Line counts come from the SAME native read — `changed_files` materializes each changed file's
two sides and counts them, so `resolveJJ` fires no `jj diff --stat` process (it used to; see
`40456bae`). Oversized and binary files report no count rather than being read whole. Cargo coverage:
`vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/working_status.rs` + `line_stats.rs`; Swift coverage:
`WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.testJJ*`.

`make app-vcs` (→ `vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh`) builds the Rust artifacts and **runs automatically
before `app-build`/`app-test`/`app-generate`** (a Makefile prerequisite). Requirements:

- **`protoc`** on PATH (`brew install protobuf`) — a build-time dep of jj-lib.
- arm64 by default; **`make app-release` builds universal** (`VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal`), which
  needs **rustup `stable` ≥ 1.93** + `rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (Homebrew's rust can't cross-compile; the script preflights this and errors clearly).
- **Unchanged inputs are a no-op.** The script hashes the Rust sources, manifests/lockfile, itself,
  `rustc --version` and the arch flavour into `vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks/.build-stamp`, and exits
  early when that matches and the outputs exist. `WR_VCS_FORCE=1 make app-vcs` rebuilds regardless.
  CI leans on this: it caches the *outputs* keyed on the same inputs, so a commit that doesn't touch
  `vcs/` skips the ~4-minute crate-graph build (and `make app-test`'s own `app-vcs` prerequisite
  stays free).
- **Xcode-driven builds are gated, not auto-fixed.** ⌘R/⌘U (and a raw `xcodebuild`) skip the
  Makefile, so they'd otherwise link the last-built core. A `Rust VCS core up to date` pre-build
  phase runs `build-apple.sh --check` and **fails the build** with `run 'make app-vcs'` when the
  stamp doesn't match `vcs/`. It can't rebuild for you: SPM extracts the binaryTarget's xcframework
  before target build phases run, so a fresh `.a` wouldn't reach that build's link. Silently linking
  a stale core cost a debugging session once — conflicted files read as `.modified` because the
  linked core predated a merged per-file-conflict fix.

The xcframework + generated Swift are **gitignored and regenerated**; only `Package.swift` + a
`shim.c` are tracked. Packaging note: the xcframework is **library-only** (no headers) and the FFI
Clang module (`wr_vcs_uniffiFFI`) is a separate SPM C target — a headers-bearing static xcframework
copies its `module.modulemap` into the shared `Debug/include/` and collides with GhosttyKit's
("Multiple commands produce include/module.modulemap").

## Formatting & linting

Swift is formatted/linted with **swift-format** (bundled with the Xcode toolchain — run via
`xcrun swift-format`, no install). Config `macapp/.swift-format` (2-space, 100 cols) covers
`WorkroomApp/` + `WorkroomAppTests/` only (not the `Scripts/*.swift` tools). Use `make app-format`
/ `make app-lint`. Every Xcode/`xcodebuild` build also runs a `swift-format lint` pre-build phase
that surfaces violations as **warnings** (non-fatal — `make app-lint` is the hard gate). Run
`make app-format` before committing.

## Gotchas

- **The Swift module is `Workroom`** (the target is `WorkroomApp`; `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` is pinned
  to `Workroom` in `project.yml`). Tests use `@testable import Workroom`. The pin matters because
  `PRODUCT_NAME` is **per-config**: `Workroom` for Release, `Workroom Dev` for Debug (see below) —
  without the pin the Debug module would become `Workroom_Dev` and break the import. A test
  target's `TEST_HOST` must point at the Debug product (`Workroom Dev.app/Contents/MacOS/Workroom
  Dev`); XcodeGen's auto-derived (target-name-based) host is wrong and fails with "Could not find
  test host".
- **Debug builds run side by side with the release build.** The Debug config has a distinct
  identity — bundle id `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, product/display name `Workroom Dev`,
  and the amber `AppIcon-Dev` icon set — so a local build doesn't fight the installed release
  `Workroom` for activation, the key window, preferences (separate UserDefaults domain via the
  bundle id), or the system-wide ⌘§ hotkey. The Debug build deliberately **doesn't register ⌘§**
  and **doesn't run Sparkle scheduled checks** (`#if DEBUG` in `WorkroomApp.swift` / `Updater.swift`)
  so it can't grab the global hotkey or try to "update" itself to the release DMG. Both builds
  still share the CLI config at `~/.config/workroom/config.json` (the bundled CLI has no
  config-path override), so they show the same projects/workrooms. `make app-run` only kills the
  `Workroom Dev` instance, never your release build. The two app icons (`make app-icon` renders
  both) are identical except for the tile gradient.
- **Adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file needs an `xcodegen generate`.** XcodeGen
  expands the source glob into explicit file refs in the (gitignored) `.xcodeproj`, so
  the change is invisible (or, for a deleted/renamed file, a hard "Build input file
  cannot be found" error) until the project is regenerated. The `make app-*` build
  targets now run `xcodegen generate` every time, so this is handled automatically —
  it only bites when building from Xcode directly (regenerate, or run `make app-generate`).
- **SourceKit "Cannot find type X in scope" is usually noise.** The single-file indexer
  doesn't see sibling files; a clean `xcodebuild` is authoritative.
- **The terminal is libghostty** (`libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework, pinned
  `exactVersion: 1.2.3` in project.yml). The embedding C API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT —
  don't float it. The terminal surface (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`) + runtime
  (`GhosttyApp`/`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`) are ours; the bundled `Resources/ghostty` (terminfo +
  shell-integration) must ship for the engine to start. Pre-GA, the plan is to move to a
  self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork.
- **The child environment has two layers, and only one of them is reliable** (`Core/ShellEnvironment.swift`).
  A Finder-launched `.app` gets a minimal PATH, so: the **floor** (`floorPath()`) reads `/etc/paths`
  + `/etc/paths.d/*` — `path_helper`'s own inputs — with no shell at all, and that alone resolves
  Postgres.app's `psql`; the **probe** (`refresh()`) then runs one `$SHELL -ilc` for what only an
  interactive login shell knows (`.zshrc` PATH entries, mise shims). The probe is best-effort by
  design: its failures degrade to the floor, so a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux` costs enrichment
  and never the bug. Three traps worth knowing: **`path_helper` APPENDS** the PATH it's handed, so
  the probe must be spawned with a *cleared* `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` or Homebrew ends
  up at the tail; the payload is a **raw `env -0` stream between UUID markers** because command
  substitution strips NULs and the user's `base64` may be GNU's (wraps at 76 cols); and the deadline
  is a `DispatchWorkItem` **inside** the blocking closure, because `withTimeout` cannot cancel a
  `runBlocking` call and would leak a shell per invocation. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once,
  in `WorkroomApp.init` — a later write would race the status sweep's `ProcessInfo.environment`
  reads. Everything else reads `ShellEnvironment.path()` (PATH only, for the automatic sweep) or
  `.environment()` (the full environment, for setup/teardown scripts).
- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.

## Layout

**VCS info that only the GUI needs** (e.g. the sidebar root row's current branch/bookmark)
is resolved app-side in `Core/BranchResolver.swift` (per project, async, with a per-call
timeout) — deliberately NOT added to the `workroom --json` contract, which the human CLI
never shows.

`WorkroomApp/Core/` — store, CLI wrapper, terminal sessions, models, theme.
`WorkroomApp/Views/` — `NavigationSplitView` tree sidebar + terminal detail.
`Scripts/` — `run.sh` (local), `build-helper.sh` (embeds+signs the Go binary), `release.sh`
(build → notarize → staple → DMG → EdDSA-sign for Sparkle), `appcast.sh` (publishes the Sparkle
appcast to the fixed `appcast` release), `appcast-notes.sh` (re-renders a published item's
`<description>` from the current release body — see "Auto-update" below), `make-icon.swift`
(regenerates the `AppIcon` PNGs in `Assets.xcassets` — run `swift Scripts/make-icon.swift`).

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

`Core/Updater.swift` wraps Sparkle's `SPUStandardUpdaterController` (the "Check for Updates…"
menu item + the Settings toggle bind to it). The `SU*` keys in `project.yml` (`SUFeedURL`,
`SUPublicEDKey`, `SUEnableAutomaticChecks`) configure it. **Versioning is tag-driven** —
`CFBundleShortVersionString`/`CFBundleVersion` resolve from `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`/
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, which `release.sh` injects from the git tag (build number =
commit count, so it only ever increases — Sparkle compares it). The appcast feed is an asset
on the fixed `appcast` GitHub release. See `README.md` ("Auto-update") for the one-time keypair
setup and the `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.

**Release channels (issue #91) — two build identities.** The **main** app (`Release` config)
switches `stable`⟷`pre` at runtime via the *Settings ▸ General ▸ Release channel* picker
(`ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` = stable/pre only). **Workroom Nightly** is a separate side-by-side
product — the `Nightly` build config in `project.yml` (bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, name, violet
`AppIcon-Nightly`, `WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL=nightly` → the `WorkroomReleaseChannel` Info.plist
marker read by `ReleaseChannel.current`/`isNightlyBuild`), extending the Debug/"Workroom Dev"
per-config identity pattern to a third identity.

`Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` returns `{nightly}` on the nightly build and the picked stable/pre
floor otherwise; one appcast feed carries all channels (`Scripts/appcast.sh` tags items via the
shared `Scripts/channel-helper.sh`; stable stays untagged = Sparkle default), and Sparkle's
bundle-id check stops either identity installing the other's DMG. Nightly is a single **rolling**
item; appcast idempotency keys on `(channel, build)`. `build-helper.sh` bakes both
`-X main.version=$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and `-X main.channel=$(WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL)` into the
bundled CLI, and `CommandLineInstaller` symlinks it as `workroom` (main) or `workroom-nightly`
(nightly build) so both coexist in PATH. `Updater.migrateReleaseChannelIfNeeded` opts an upgrading
beta user into `pre` and coerces a legacy `.nightly` selection to `.stable` (main build only).

**Release-notes in the update dialog.** Sparkle's dialog renders the appcast item's
`<description>`. `appcast.sh` (run during the release) embeds the GitHub release body as that
description — but at release time the body is still goreleaser's raw commit list, since the
curated notes are written afterwards. So a second path keeps them in sync: the
`.github/workflows/appcast-notes.yml` workflow fires on every `release: edited` event and runs
`Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`, which re-renders the matching item's `<description>` from the
release's *current* body. Curating a release's notes therefore auto-refreshes what the update
dialog shows; no rebuild needed. To fix an already-published feed by hand, run it directly:
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) macapp/Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

149	  /// area (i.e. still over the strip → a reorder, not a drop-into-pane).
150	  private func chipLocal(_ global: CGPoint) -> CGPoint? {
151	    guard contentFrame.contains(global) else { return nil }

157	  private func chipDropTarget(at global: CGPoint) -> (tab: TerminalTab.ID, edge: PaneEdge)? {

149	          showLeadingSeparator: showsLeadingSeparator(at: index),
150	          isGrouped: groupMembers.contains(tab.id),
151	          agentBadge: agentBadge, onAgentTap: { agentPopoverTab = tab.id }
152	        ) {
153	          store.requestCloseTerminalTab(tab.id, for: target)
154	        }
155	        .popover(
156	          isPresented: Binding(
157	            get: { agentPopoverTab == tab.id },
158	            set: { if !$0 { agentPopoverTab = nil } })
159	        ) {
160	          agentPopover(for: tab)
161	        }
162	        .onHover { inside in
163	          if inside { hoveredTab = tab.id } else if hoveredTab == tab.id { hoveredTab = nil }
164	        }
165	        .onTapGesture {
166	          // Eager: select on the first click (changes `active.id`; the view's .onChange hook
167	          // marks the tab read). A quick second click on the same chip promotes a preview content
168	          // tab to persisted (#66) — `persist` no-ops on terminal/persisted tabs, so this is safe
169	          // for every chip and never delays the select.
170	          let now = Date()
171	          sessions.select(tab.id, for: target)
172	          if let last = lastChipClick, last.id == tab.id, now.timeIntervalSince(last.at) < 0.35 {
173	            sessions.persist(tab.id, for: target)
174	            lastChipClick = nil
175	          } else {
176	            lastChipClick = ChipClick(id: tab.id, at: now)
177	          }
178	        }
179	        .tabChipContextMenu(tab: tab, target: target, store: store, sessions: sessions)
180	        // Measure in .global space: a .local drag reads coordinates relative to the
181	        // chip, which itself moves via .offset(dragTranslation) — that feedback loop
182	        // dampens the translation so the chip lags the cursor. Global space is fixed.
183	        .gesture(
184	          DragGesture(minimumDistance: 6, coordinateSpace: .global)
185	            .onChanged { value in
186	              if draggingID == nil { draggingID = tab.id }
187	              guard draggingID == tab.id else { return }
188	              dragTranslation = value.translation.width
189	              // Dragged down over the pane area → preview a drop-into-pane (the strip stops gapping).
190	              chipPaneDrag = localize(value.location)
191	                .map { PaneDragState(tabID: tab.id, location: $0) }
192	            }
193	            .onEnded { value in
194	              if let drop = dropTarget(value.location) {
195	                sessions.moveTabIntoSplit(
196	                  tab.id, ontoEdge: drop.edge, of: drop.tab, for: target)
197	                draggingID = nil
198	                dragTranslation = 0
199	              } else {
200	                commitDrag()  // a plain strip reorder
201	              }
202	              chipPaneDrag = nil
203	            }
204	        )
205	        .offset(x: offsetX)
206	        .zIndex(isDragging ? 1 : 0)
207	        .animation(
208	          isDragging || reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.18), value: offsetX
209	        )
210	        // Scroll target for `OverflowingTabScroller`'s `ScrollViewReader` (issue #129 follow-up) — the
211	        // same id `ForEach` already keys identity on.
212	        .id(tab.id)
213	      }
214	      // A divider sets the new-terminal (+) button apart from the last tab (mirrors the workroom
215	      // tab bar). Hidden when the last tab is set apart on its own — focused or hovered — to match
216	      // the "no divider beside the focused/hovered tab" rule above, and when the "+" has pinned
217	      // (issue #129): the fade and the gutter already separate the two regions, and a hairline beside
218	      // a dissolving edge reads as a cut. Toggled via OPACITY (not removed) so it stays laid out and
219	      // the "+" never shifts as the hover/focus comes and goes — which also keeps the measured run
220	      // width stable across those transitions.
221	      // Only present at all with ≥1 tab (a split member's empty strip is just the "+" and close ✕).
222	      // Negative leading trims the gap to the last tab to ~2pt (HStack `tabSpacing` 4 − 2), matching
223	      // the inter-tab dividers.
224	      if !tabs.isEmpty {
225	        Rectangle()
226	          .fill(ThemeService.shared.tokens.border)
227	          .frame(width: 1, height: 14)
228	          .padding(.leading, -2)
229	          .padding(.trailing, 4)
230	          .opacity(showsTrailingDivider && !overflowing ? 1 : 0)
231	      }
232	    }
233	    .background(alignment: .leading) { splitWell(tabs) }
234	    .onPreferenceChange(TabWidthKey.self) { widths = $0 }

156	  /// The two-column `NavigationSplitView` core (sidebar + detail/inspector). The window chrome, modal
157	  /// presentations, and lifecycle hooks layer on in `body` via the `root*` helpers below — each its own
158	  /// function so the modifier chain type-checks within the compiler's budget. The fully-inline chain
159	  /// timed out the type-checker on CI ("unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time"); this
160	  /// is the same split-it-up reason `EdgeRevealSidebars`/`MenuStateValues`/`NewWorkroomPresenter` exist.
161	  private var splitView: some View {
162	    // A hand-rolled split (sidebar | detail | inspector) instead of `NavigationSplitView`: the native
163	    // sidebar column drew an inset card with a ~30pt top toolbar-reserve that left an empty gap under
164	    // the custom title bar, and that inset isn't controllable. `SidebarColumn`/`InspectorColumn` are
165	    // our own resizable cards (same `sidebarCard` as the edge-reveal, so pinned == unpinned), giving
166	    // full control over their position. Visibility round-trips through `store.sidebarVisible` /
167	    // `showInspector` (the View-menu ticks + toggles); width persists per column to `Defaults`.
168	    // A *detail-only* NavigationSplitView: we keep it (vs a plain HStack) only for the window
169	    // toolbar/layering context it sets up — that's what lets the custom title bar, drawn in the
170	    // full-size content under the native title bar, render crisp instead of washed-out by the
171	    // title-bar vibrancy (a plain HStack / NavigationStack doesn't). Its native sidebar column is
172	    // never used (forced `.detailOnly`) — that column is what kept the ~30pt inset-card top gap — so
173	    // the real sidebar is our own `SidebarColumn` in the detail HStack, flush below the bar.
174	    // Wrapped in a *detail-only* `NavigationSplitView` (empty sidebar column, forced `.detailOnly`) —
175	    // NOT a plain HStack. A plain HStack detail in a full-size-content window with a visible `.unified`
176	    // toolbar loses SwiftUI `.onHover` for its content that sits near the top under the title bar (the
177	    // terminal tab strip's trailing toolbar buttons never lit their hover well — issue #114); the
178	    // title-bar region eats mouse-moved for a raw content view. `NavigationSplitView` hosts the detail
179	    // in an `NSSplitViewController`, which sets up the correct content tracking so `.onHover` fires
180	    // again. Dropping it (0e354d6e) was to stop it clipping `.toolbar { items }` to the sidebar-column
181	    // width — but the chrome no longer lives in toolbar items; it's a full-width window-level `.left`
182	    // `TitlebarAccessoryHost` (see `accessoryBarContent`), which NavigationSplitView does not clip. So
183	    // we get correct hover back with no clipping. The empty native sidebar column is unused — the real
184	    // sidebar is our own `SidebarColumn` in the detail HStack, flush below the bar.
185	    NavigationSplitView(columnVisibility: .constant(.detailOnly)) {
186	      Color.clear.frame(width: 0)
187	    } detail: {
188	      HStack(spacing: 0) {
189	        if store.sidebarVisible {
190	          SidebarColumn(
191	            paneDrag: $workroomChipDrag,
192	            localize: { workroomChipLocal($0) },
193	            dropTarget: { workroomChipDropTarget(at: $0) }
194	          )
195	          .transition(.move(edge: .leading))
196	        }
197	        detail
198	          .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
199	        if showInspector {
200	          InspectorColumn()
201	            .transition(.move(edge: .trailing))
202	        }
203	        // The activity bar is ALWAYS present, flush to the window's trailing edge — the inspector
204	        // content pane (above) slides in/out beside it. Placed inside the detail-only
205	        // NavigationSplitView so its icon buttons get working `.onHover` (issue #114).
206	        ActivityBar()
207	      }
208	      .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: store.sidebarVisible)
209	      .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: showInspector)
210	    }
211	  }

3	/// Hover/press chrome for the title-bar toolbar's icon buttons (sidebar toggle, back/forward, quick
4	/// terminal, run/stop/restart, bell, inspector toggle). Replaces the bare `.borderless` style so they
5	/// get the SAME affordance as every other icon button in the app — the sidebar's theme/add buttons and
6	/// the tab strips' "+" all use a `tokens.hover` rounded square on hover — instead of no feedback at all.
7	///
8	/// A `ButtonStyle` (not a per-button `.onHover` + manual background) so one modifier on each title-bar
9	/// bar covers all its buttons, including nested ones, and the hover rect sizes itself to each glyph.
10	struct ToolbarIconButtonStyle: ButtonStyle {
11	  func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
12	    Chrome(configuration: configuration)
13	  }
14	
15	  /// A view (not an inline modifier chain) so it can hold the `@State hovering` a `ButtonStyle`'s
16	  /// `Configuration` doesn't carry, and read `isEnabled` to suppress hover on a disabled button.
17	  private struct Chrome: View {
18	    let configuration: Configuration
19	    @Environment(\.isEnabled) private var isEnabled
20	    @State private var hovering = false
21	    private let theme = ThemeService.shared
22	
23	    var body: some View {
24	      configuration.label
25	        // A uniform tap target so every glyph gets the same square hover well, matching the sidebar's
26	        // 28pt buttons in spirit while staying compact enough for the 28pt-tall title-bar row.
27	        .frame(minWidth: 22, minHeight: 22)
28	        .padding(.horizontal, 3)
29	        .background(
30	          // Animate ONLY the hover fill's opacity — never the whole button. A view-tree
31	          // `.animation(.easeOut, value: hovering)` at the end of this chain would also animate the
32	          // *label's* layout: on hover-in the glyph's pixel-snapped origin can re-round by one device
33	          // pixel (release/optimized builds and fractional display scaling snap differently than a
34	          // Debug build on an integer-scale display), and the implicit animation interpolates that 1pt
35	          // re-round into a visible "slide then settle" of the icon (issue #78). Scoping the animation
36	          // to the fill keeps the glyph out of every animation transaction, so any re-round snaps
37	          // instantly and imperceptibly while the well still fades in.
38	          RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6, style: .continuous)
39	            .fill(theme.tokens.hover)
40	            .opacity(hovering && isEnabled ? 1 : 0)
41	            .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.12), value: hovering)
42	        )
43	        .contentShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6, style: .continuous))
44	        // Dim on press; dim further when disabled — restoring what `.borderless` gave. Without the
45	        // disabled case a disabled button (e.g. Back/Forward with no history) renders at full strength,
46	        // so it looks active yet never shows a hover well — reading as a broken/"missing" hover. The
47	        // dim makes "disabled, so no hover" legible; enabled buttons keep the hover fill.
48	        .opacity(configuration.isPressed ? 0.6 : (isEnabled ? 1 : 0.4))
49	        .onHover { hovering = $0 }
50	    }
51	  }
52	}

<!-- /autoplan restore point: none — no prior plan file existed (fresh plan from issue #139) -->

# Issue #139 — Always show the workroom title bar and toolbar

## Context

Today a workroom only gets its own chrome when it is part of a **split group**. `WorkroomPaneLeaf`
(`macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:140`) gates a header + card underlay behind
`multi` (`leaves.count >= 2`, line 51): a `project / workroom` title bar with the remove-from-split
✕, and a rounded, tinted, shadowed card beneath the whole pane. A solo workroom gets none of it —
its terminal tab strip sits bare at the top of the detail area.

Meanwhile the workroom's own actions live in the **window titlebar**: `TrailingTitlebarBar`
(`Views/TitlebarBars.swift:162-169`) renders `OpenInControl` + `RunControls` keyed on
`store.selectedTarget`. That is the wrong home for them twice over:

- **They are workroom-scoped controls in window-scoped chrome.** In a split, the visible members
  each have a path and a run state, but only the *selected* one is reachable from the titlebar.
- **The titlebar is out of room and out of context.** Workroom UI has nowhere to grow (issue #139
  names run + "Open in…" as the first movers).

The outcome: every workroom, split or not, renders as a self-contained card with its own title bar
and its own trailing toolbar. The window titlebar keeps only global chrome. Because the header is
then unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` loses most of its `multi` branching rather than gaining more.

**Premises confirmed (D1):** header always on, pixel-identical solo vs split; run + "Open in…" move
out of the titlebar entirely and become per-workroom; the titlebar keeps sidebar toggle,
back/forward, workroom tab chips, update pill, Quick Terminal.

**Design calls confirmed:** solo card uses the *same* geometry as a split member — 6pt outer gutter
+ 4pt inset (D2); solo renders accent-tinted, i.e. as a focused member (D3); the header toolbar
keeps `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`, so the moved buttons look exactly as they do today (D4).

---

## The shape of the change

```
BEFORE                                    AFTER
window titlebar                           window titlebar
 ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd                ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd
 ├ workroom tab chips                      ├ workroom tab chips
 └ update · OpenIn · Run · QuickTerm       └ update · QuickTerm
                                                    (workroom controls gone)
detail (solo)          detail (split)     detail (solo AND split — one shape)
┌──────────────────┐   ┌──────┐┌──────┐   ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ [tab][tab] +  ⧈ ⧉│   │ hdr ✕││ hdr ✕│   │ ⬛ project / room   ⏵ ⧉  [✕]  │ ← always
│ ░░ terminal ░░░░ │   │[tab] ││[tab] │   ├────────────────────────────────┤
└──────────────────┘   │ ░░░░ ││ ░░░░ │   │ [tab][tab] +          ⧈ ⧉ ⊠   │
  no card, 2pt gutter  └──────┘└──────┘   │ ░░░ terminal ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │
                        cards, 6+4        └────────────────────────────────┘
                                            card + 6pt outer / 4pt inset
                                            [✕] = remove-from-split, multi only
```

`multi` survives in exactly three places (all leaf-level, none structural for the terminal):
the remove-from-split ✕, the context menu's "Remove from Split" item, and the group-drag gesture.

---

## Implementation

### 1. `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift` — the header becomes unconditional

**`WorkroomPaneLeaf.body` (line 140-218).** Drop the `if multi` around the header (line 150). The
long comment at 140-148 explains why the header must stay a *sibling* above `content` and never a
wrapper — that constraint is now satisfied more strongly than before: with no `if`, there is no
`_ConditionalContent` branch to flip when a 2-member split dissolves, so the libghostty
re-parent/blank hazard for this axis disappears outright. **Keep the `VStack(spacing: 0) { titleBar;
content }` shape exactly; do not restructure it.**

- `.gesture(...)` (161-174) stays attached but becomes mask-gated:
  `.gesture(dragGesture, including: multi ? .all : .none)` — a value-level switch, not a structural
  `if`. (Solo, the gesture is inert anyway: `dropHighlight` filters `hit.tab != drag.sid` and
  `onEnded` filters `drop.sid != sid`. Masking it is honesty, not a fix.)
- `.contextMenu` (182-186) stays attached always — Close / Set Label / Delete are useful solo.
  Pass `onRemoveFromSplit: multi ? onClose : nil`; `workroomContextMenu`
  (`Views/WorkroomContextMenu.swift:37`) already omits the item (and its divider, line 50) on `nil`.
- Card modifiers (196-213): delete every `multi ? … : …` ternary. Fill becomes
  `focused ? splitGroupFocusedFill : splitGroupFill`, `panel`, `cornerRadius: 8`, the
  focused/unfocused shadow, and `EdgeInsets(4,4,4,4)` unconditionally. A solo leaf is *always* the
  selected one (`RootView.workroomSplitBody` passes `focusedID: selected` and
  `layout: .leaf(selected)`), so `focused` is already `true` solo — **D3's accent tint needs no
  special case.**
- `content(compact: multi)` (190) → `content()`; see §3.
- `.accessibilityAddTraits(focused && multi ? .isSelected : [])` (217): keep the `multi` term.
  Solo has nothing to select *between*, and `pane-isSelected-is-model-focus-not-first-responder`
  says this trait is already load-bearing for tests as a model-focus signal — widening it would
  make every solo pane report selected.

**`WorkroomSplitView.body` (line 83).** `.padding(.horizontal, multi ? 6 : 0)` → `.padding(.horizontal, 6)`.

**`WorkroomSplitGroupTitleBar` (line 264-317)** gains a trailing toolbar and per-member state. New
stored properties: `target: TerminalTarget`, `multi: Bool`. Trailing run replaces the bare
`CloseWorkroomPaneButton` (298):

```swift
Spacer(minLength: 8)
HStack(spacing: 6) {
  if !isMissing {
    OpenInControl(path: target.path)
    if let projectPath = AppStore.projectPath(of: sid) {
      RunControls(target: target, projectPath: projectPath)
    }
  }
}
.buttonStyle(ToolbarIconButtonStyle())     // D4 — same chrome as the titlebar today
if multi {
  TitlebarDivider()
  CloseWorkroomPaneButton(action: onClose)  // brings its own .plain style
}
```

Rename the type to `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` (it is no longer split-specific) and update its doc
comment; keep `accessibilityIdentifier("workroom.pane.titlebar")` unchanged — `SplitPaneUITests`
queries it in six tests.

Two things to get right here:

- **`RunControls` declares `@EnvironmentObject var store`, and that is fine.** SwiftUI invalidates
  only the view that declares the dependency, so putting it *inside* the header does **not**
  subscribe `WorkroomPaneLeaf` (or the terminal subtree below it) to store churn — the invariant at
  `WorkroomSplitView.swift:23-26,124-127` holds. The environment object is in scope: `RootView`
  injects it for the whole `splitView` tree.
- **Hover.** `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` and `OpenInControl`'s `Menu` both need live `.onHover`.
  The detail is inside the `NavigationSplitView` that exists precisely to keep `.onHover` working
  near the top of the content (`RootView.swift:174-184`, issue #114) — the header sits below the
  titlebar accessory, in that content. Verify with a **real mouse**, not a synthetic event.

### 2. `Core/AppStore.swift` — Run must act on the passed target, not the selection

`RunControls`' Run button calls `store.runOrFocusRunCommand()` (line 1630), which reads
`selectedTarget`. Per-workroom buttons make that wrong: clicking Run on a **non-focused split
member** would start the run in the *focused* workroom. Root-cause fix — split the method:

```swift
/// ⌘R / menu: act on the current selection. Suppressed while a text field is being edited.
func runOrFocusRunCommand() {
  guard !isEditingTextField, let target = selectedTarget else { return }
  runOrFocusRunCommand(for: target)
}

/// The per-target state machine (the diagram at 1603-1629 moves here). A workroom's own Run
/// button calls this directly with ITS target.
func runOrFocusRunCommand(for target: TerminalTarget) {
  guard !target.isMissing else { return }
  … existing switch body, unchanged …
}
```

`isEditingTextField` stays on the *keyboard/selection* wrapper only. That is deliberate and fixes a
latent bug: today a Run **click** while the sidebar filter or the Project Settings command field
holds focus silently no-ops, because a button press was routed through a guard written for ⌘R
(comment at 1593-1597 says as much — "the ambient ⌘R … must not fire behind an editor"). `Stop` and
`Restart` already take a target (`stopRunCommand(for:)` 1711, `restartRunCommand(for:)` 1726) and
carry no such guard, so the three buttons become consistent.

Leave `toggleRunCommand(for:)` (1583, the sidebar row toggle) alone — different semantics
(start/stop, no focus, no single-owner hop).

### 3. Delete the `compact` axis (D2 makes it dead)

With solo and split geometry identical, `compact` is permanently `true`. Remove the parameter and
inline the compact values — a live-looking branch that can only take one value is worse than no
branch:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:190,235` | `content(compact:)` → `content()` |
| `Views/TargetTerminalDetail.swift:19,27` | drop `var compact` and the pass-through |
| `Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:21,59-60,86` | drop `var compact`; padding becomes `.horizontal, 2` / `.bottom, 2` |
| `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:24,63` | drop `var compact`; `leadingInset` becomes `4` |

Rewrite the comments those numbers carry (they currently explain the solo-vs-split difference) to
state the single rule: the terminal sits 2pt inside its workroom card, and the leftmost tab lines up
with the terminal panel below it. `RootView.swift:658`'s `WorkroomTerminalsView(target:sessions:)`
fallback needs no edit (it never passed `compact`).

### 4. `Views/TitlebarBars.swift` — the titlebar loses the workroom controls

Delete the `if let target = store.selectedTarget, !target.isMissing { … }` block
(`TrailingTitlebarBar`, 162-169) with its `OpenInControl`, `RunControls`, and trailing
`TitlebarDivider`. What remains: the update pill (+ its divider) and Quick Terminal. Update the
struct's doc comment (140-143) — it currently advertises "the selected target's run/open-in
actions".

**Nothing else moves.** The Run menu (`WorkroomApp.swift:939-949`), Go ▸ "Open in …"
(`1082-1086`), the `AppDelegate` ⌘R/⌥⌘R/⇧⌘R monitor (`267-288`), and the
`hasRunCommand`/`canOpenInEditor` `focusedSceneValue`s all keep acting on the selection through the
unchanged selection-scoped entry points.

### 5. `Views/TargetDetailToolbar.swift` — accessibility identifiers + docs

`OpenInControl` has no `accessibilityIdentifier` on either control (only dynamic
`accessibilityLabel`s — `"Open in \(name)"`, `"Choose editor"`), which is why it has zero UI-test
coverage today. Add stable ids following the dotted convention: `openIn.primary` and `openIn.menu`.
Update both doc comments (9-14, 67-71) — they say "composes into the title-bar toolbar
(`TrailingTitlebarBar`)"; the host is now the workroom pane title bar. `RunControls` keeps
`runCommand.run` / `.stop` / `.restart` verbatim (six existing UI tests query them).

---

## Verification

**Build gate** (`make app-*` must run with the command sandbox disabled):

```bash
make app-format && make app-lint && make app-build && make app-test
```

Read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via `xcresulttool` — `make app-test` hides the summary under
Xcode 26. No files are added or removed, so no `xcodegen` surprises.

**Unit tests** (`WorkroomAppTests`)

- `RunCommandTests`: add coverage that `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` acts on the **passed** target
  while a *different* target is selected (start, focus-existing, stopped→re-run, and the
  single-owner-elsewhere hop). Assert the selection-based overload still delegates.
- `WorkroomSplitTests` / `PaneLayoutTests`: unchanged — the model is untouched. Run them to prove it.

**UI tests** (`WorkroomAppUITests`, own scheme; scope with
`xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/<Class>/<method>` — `make app-uitest` ignores
`APP_TEST_FLAGS`, and never run the whole suite)

- New in `SplitPaneUITests` (or a new `WorkroomPaneHeaderUITests`), default fixture = solo:
  1. `workroom.pane.titlebar` exists with **no** split flags, and its label is `project, workroom …`.
  2. `workroom.pane.close` does **not** exist solo; it **does** with `-WorkroomUITestWorkroomSplit 1`.
  3. `runCommand.run` is inside the pane header: scope the query to the `workroom.pane` element

# Issue #139 — Always show the workroom title bar and toolbar

## Context

Today a workroom only gets its own chrome when it is part of a **split group**. `WorkroomPaneLeaf`
(`macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:140`) gates a header + card underlay behind
`multi` (`leaves.count >= 2`, line 51): a `project / workroom` title bar with the remove-from-split
✕, and a rounded, tinted, shadowed card beneath the whole pane. A solo workroom gets none of it —
its terminal tab strip sits bare at the top of the detail area.

Meanwhile the workroom's own actions live in the **window titlebar**: `TrailingTitlebarBar`
(`Views/TitlebarBars.swift:162-169`) renders `OpenInControl` + `RunControls` keyed on
`store.selectedTarget`. That is the wrong home for them twice over:

- **They are workroom-scoped controls in window-scoped chrome.** In a split, the visible members
  each have a path and a run state, but only the *selected* one is reachable from the titlebar.
- **The titlebar is out of room and out of context.** Workroom UI has nowhere to grow (issue #139
  names run + "Open in…" as the first movers).

The outcome: every workroom, split or not, renders as a self-contained card with its own title bar
and its own trailing toolbar. The window titlebar keeps only global chrome. Because the header is
then unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` loses most of its `multi` branching rather than gaining more.

**Premises confirmed (D1):** header always on, pixel-identical solo vs split; run + "Open in…" move
out of the titlebar entirely and become per-workroom; the titlebar keeps sidebar toggle,
back/forward, workroom tab chips, update pill, Quick Terminal.

**Design calls confirmed:** solo card uses the *same* geometry as a split member — 6pt outer gutter
+ 4pt inset (D2); solo renders accent-tinted, i.e. as a focused member (D3); the header toolbar
keeps `ToolbarIconButtonStyle`, so the moved buttons look exactly as they do today (D4).

---

## The shape of the change

```
BEFORE                                    AFTER
window titlebar                           window titlebar
 ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd                ├ sidebar toggle, back/fwd
 ├ workroom tab chips                      ├ workroom tab chips
 └ update · OpenIn · Run · QuickTerm       └ update · QuickTerm
                                                    (workroom controls gone)
detail (solo)          detail (split)     detail (solo AND split — one shape)
┌──────────────────┐   ┌──────┐┌──────┐   ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ [tab][tab] +  ⧈ ⧉│   │ hdr ✕││ hdr ✕│   │ ⬛ project / room   ⏵ ⧉  [✕]  │ ← always
│ ░░ terminal ░░░░ │   │[tab] ││[tab] │   ├────────────────────────────────┤
└──────────────────┘   │ ░░░░ ││ ░░░░ │   │ [tab][tab] +          ⧈ ⧉ ⊠   │
  no card, 2pt gutter  └──────┘└──────┘   │ ░░░ terminal ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │
                        cards, 6+4        └────────────────────────────────┘
                                            card + 6pt outer / 4pt inset
                                            [✕] = remove-from-split, multi only
```

`multi` survives in exactly three places (all leaf-level, none structural for the terminal):
the remove-from-split ✕, the context menu's "Remove from Split" item, and the group-drag gesture.

---

## Implementation

### 1. `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift` — the header becomes unconditional

**`WorkroomPaneLeaf.body` (line 140-218).** Drop the `if multi` around the header (line 150). The
long comment at 140-148 explains why the header must stay a *sibling* above `content` and never a
wrapper — that constraint is now satisfied more strongly than before: with no `if`, there is no
`_ConditionalContent` branch to flip when a 2-member split dissolves, so the libghostty
re-parent/blank hazard for this axis disappears outright. **Keep the `VStack(spacing: 0) { titleBar;
content }` shape exactly; do not restructure it.**

- `.gesture(...)` (161-174) stays attached but becomes mask-gated:
  `.gesture(dragGesture, including: multi ? .all : .none)` — a value-level switch, not a structural
  `if`. (Solo, the gesture is inert anyway: `dropHighlight` filters `hit.tab != drag.sid` and
  `onEnded` filters `drop.sid != sid`. Masking it is honesty, not a fix.)
- `.contextMenu` (182-186) stays attached always — Close / Set Label / Delete are useful solo.
  Pass `onRemoveFromSplit: multi ? onClose : nil`; `workroomContextMenu`
  (`Views/WorkroomContextMenu.swift:37`) already omits the item (and its divider, line 50) on `nil`.
- Card modifiers (196-213): delete every `multi ? … : …` ternary. Fill becomes
  `focused ? splitGroupFocusedFill : splitGroupFill`, `panel`, `cornerRadius: 8`, the
  focused/unfocused shadow, and `EdgeInsets(4,4,4,4)` unconditionally. A solo leaf is *always* the
  selected one (`RootView.workroomSplitBody` passes `focusedID: selected` and
  `layout: .leaf(selected)`), so `focused` is already `true` solo — **D3's accent tint needs no
  special case.**

  Solo has nothing to select *between*, and `pane-isSelected-is-model-focus-not-first-responder`
  says this trait is already load-bearing for tests as a model-focus signal — widening it would
  make every solo pane report selected.

**`WorkroomSplitView.body` (line 83).** `.padding(.horizontal, multi ? 6 : 0)` → `.padding(.horizontal, 6)`.

Spacer(minLength: 8)
HStack(spacing: 6) {

}

queries it in six tests.

  injects it for the whole `splitView` tree.

  The detail is inside the `NavigationSplitView` that exists precisely to keep `.onHover` working
  near the top of the content (`RootView.swift:174-184`, issue #114) — the header sits below the
  titlebar accessory, in that content. Verify with a **real mouse**, not a synthetic event.

### 2. `Core/AppStore.swift` — Run must act on the passed target, not the selection

`RunControls`' Run button calls `store.runOrFocusRunCommand()` (line 1630), which reads
`selectedTarget`. Per-workroom buttons make that wrong: clicking Run on a **non-focused split
member** would start the run in the *focused* workroom. Root-cause fix — split the method:

```swift
/// ⌘R / menu: act on the current selection. Suppressed while a text field is being edited.
func runOrFocusRunCommand() {
  guard !isEditingTextField, let target = selectedTarget else { return }
  runOrFocusRunCommand(for: target)
}

/// The per-target state machine (the diagram at 1603-1629 moves here). A workroom's own Run
/// button calls this directly with ITS target.
func runOrFocusRunCommand(for target: TerminalTarget) {
  guard !target.isMissing else { return }
  … existing switch body, unchanged …
}
```

`isEditingTextField` stays on the *keyboard/selection* wrapper only. That is deliberate and fixes a
latent bug: today a Run **click** while the sidebar filter or the Project Settings command field
holds focus silently no-ops, because a button press was routed through a guard written for ⌘R
(comment at 1593-1597 says as much — "the ambient ⌘R … must not fire behind an editor"). `Stop` and
`Restart` already take a target (`stopRunCommand(for:)` 1711, `restartRunCommand(for:)` 1726) and
carry no such guard, so the three buttons become consistent.

Leave `toggleRunCommand(for:)` (1583, the sidebar row toggle) alone — different semantics
(start/stop, no focus, no single-owner hop).

### 3. Delete the `compact` axis (D2 makes it dead)

With solo and split geometry identical, `compact` is permanently `true`. Remove the parameter and
inline the compact values — a live-looking branch that can only take one value is worse than no
branch:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:190,235` | `content(compact:)` → `content()` |
| `Views/TargetTerminalDetail.swift:19,27` | drop `var compact` and the pass-through |
| `Views/WorkroomTerminalsView.swift:21,59-60,86` | drop `var compact`; padding becomes `.horizontal, 2` / `.bottom, 2` |
| `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:24,63` | drop `var compact`; `leadingInset` becomes `4` |

Rewrite the comments those numbers carry (they currently explain the solo-vs-split difference) to
state the single rule: the terminal sits 2pt inside its workroom card, and the leftmost tab lines up
with the terminal panel below it. `RootView.swift:658`'s `WorkroomTerminalsView(target:sessions:)`
fallback needs no edit (it never passed `compact`).

### 4. `Views/TitlebarBars.swift` — the titlebar loses the workroom controls

Delete the `if let target = store.selectedTarget, !target.isMissing { … }` block
(`TrailingTitlebarBar`, 162-169) with its `OpenInControl`, `RunControls`, and trailing
`TitlebarDivider`. What remains: the update pill (+ its divider) and Quick Terminal. Update the
struct's doc comment (140-143) — it currently advertises "the selected target's run/open-in
actions".

**Nothing else moves.** The Run menu (`WorkroomApp.swift:939-949`), Go ▸ "Open in …"
(`1082-1086`), the `AppDelegate` ⌘R/⌥⌘R/⇧⌘R monitor (`267-288`), and the
`hasRunCommand`/`canOpenInEditor` `focusedSceneValue`s all keep acting on the selection through the
unchanged selection-scoped entry points.

### 5. `Views/TargetDetailToolbar.swift` — accessibility identifiers + docs

`OpenInControl` has no `accessibilityIdentifier` on either control (only dynamic
`accessibilityLabel`s — `"Open in \(name)"`, `"Choose editor"`), which is why it has zero UI-test
coverage today. Add stable ids following the dotted convention: `openIn.primary` and `openIn.menu`.
Update both doc comments (9-14, 67-71) — they say "composes into the title-bar toolbar
(`TrailingTitlebarBar`)"; the host is now the workroom pane title bar. `RunControls` keeps
`runCommand.run` / `.stop` / `.restart` verbatim (six existing UI tests query them).
