```
⬛ project / room     [⟳][■] │ [icon ⌄] │ ⧉
                      run    div open-in  ✕
```

**Divider added, and it hides properly.** The subtle part: `RunControls` renders *nothing* when no run command is configured, and `OpenInControl` renders nothing when no supported editor is installed — so the header couldn't see whether either group was actually there. A divider gated on "should there be run buttons" would have left a stray rule on a project with no run command.

Fixed by moving both facts into `WorkroomPaneToolbarPresentation` as inputs and deriving `divider = run && openIn` in the same pass. It now can't disagree with the buttons on either side. The leaf resolves it (it has the store); the title bar stays store-free as before. Two new tests cover both empty sides.

**Yes, the icon can be bigger — 18 → 20.** The 22pt well was never the constraint: `ToolbarIconButtonStyle` sets `minWidth`/`minHeight`, so the well grows with its label. The real ceiling is the title bar's 28pt row:

- **24pt** — 2pt clearance, safe
- **26pt** — 1pt, tight
- **>28pt** — clips, or the row has to grow

Above ~22pt the icon starts filling the hover well edge to edge, so the well stops reading as a well. I went to 20 for a visible bump with room left; the headroom is documented on the constant so the next person doesn't assume 22 is a cap. Say a number if you want it pushed further.

The action already existed — `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)`'s no-command branch has opened Project Settings with the warning since issue #127. It was just unreachable by click, because every Run button hid itself behind `canRunCommand`. So this widened an existing path rather than adding one.

**Removed the gate:** `RunControls` now renders for any present target; `hasRunCommand` is gone from the presentation inputs entirely, so the run group can only be hidden by a missing directory or a target with no owning project. That's deliberate — with no parameter to pass, nobody can reintroduce the gate by accident.

**Sidebar left alone.** Its per-row buttons still hide behind `canRunCommand`. A list of many workrooms each showing a button that only opens a settings sheet would be noise; a single header button that teaches you how to configure one is the opposite.

**One thing I added unasked:** the tooltip. It said "Run the project command (⌘R)" — a lie when the click opens settings instead. Now it swaps to "No run command configured — set one in Project Settings (⌘R)". Revert it if you'd rather it stayed constant.

Also updated the AppStore comment that asserted this branch was keyboard-only (now false), and the `testCanRunCommandGate` doc, which claimed "no command → no run controls" — still true for the sidebar, no longer for the header.

**Tests:** presentation matrix reworked (`testRunIsNotGatedOnAConfiguredCommand` proves the input is gone), plus a UI test clicking the header's Run with `-WorkroomUITestNoRunCommand 1` and asserting the warned sheet appears. It's a separate test from the ⌘R one on purpose — the keyboard goes through the selection overload, the click through the per-target one.

Build ✓, lint ✓, **1374 passed / 0 failed**.

## The frame was never sizing the icon

The control was built as a hidden SF Symbol with the real icon overlaid on it:

```swift
Image(systemName: "arrow.up.forward.app")
  .hidden()
  .overlay { Image(nsImage: remembered.icon)... }
  .frame(width: 20, height: 20)   // ← did nothing to the icon
```

An `.overlay` takes the size of the view it's attached to, and a bare `Image` is fixed-size — it reports its intrinsic size no matter what's proposed. So the icon rendered at whatever the ambient **font** made the hidden symbol (~13pt), and the `.frame` just centred that 13pt icon inside a larger transparent box.

Which means it was never 16, never 18, never 20. It's been ~13pt the whole time, and all three of my "bigger" edits changed a box nobody could see. That's on me — I changed the number and reported it without a way to confirm the number was load-bearing.

Fixed by sizing the icon itself:

```swift
Image(nsImage: remembered.icon)
  .renderingMode(.original)
  .resizable()
  .scaledToFit()
  .frame(width: PaneToolbarIcon.appIcon, height: PaneToolbarIcon.appIcon)
```

**It also explains the original complaint.** At 13pt, app-icon artwork carries ~20% transparent margin, so ~10pt of visible glyph sat next to 13pt symbols that fill their box. Genuinely much smaller, exactly as you said.

Now at 20pt it should be plainly bigger. Two numbers worth knowing, both now on the constant:

- **~16-17pt** = exact optical parity with the 13pt symbols (13 ÷ 0.8)
- **22pt** = the real ceiling. The well is a `minWidth`, so anything above 22 grows *this* button's well while the run buttons stay 22 — it'd become visibly taller than its neighbours

20 is deliberately past parity so it reads as the group's primary action. Say a number if you want it dialled back.

feat(macapp): give every workroom its own title bar and toolbar

Closes #139.

A workroom only had its own chrome when it was part of a split group, and its
run/"Open in…" controls lived in the window title bar keyed on the *selected*
target — so a co-displayed split member's were unreachable, and
`runOrFocusRunCommand()` read the selection, meaning a per-member Run button
would have started the run in the wrong workroom.

Now every workroom renders as a card with its own header and its own trailing
toolbar, and the window title bar keeps only window-level chrome (sidebar
toggle, back/forward, workroom chips, update pill, Quick Terminal).

Because the header became unconditional, `WorkroomPaneLeaf` LOST most of its
`multi` branching rather than gaining more: with no `if` there is no
`_ConditionalContent` branch left to flip when a split dissolves, so the
libghostty re-parent hazard on that axis is gone. `multi` now survives in four
leaf-level places only — the remove-from-split ✕, its menu item, the group-drag
gesture mask, and the a11y `.isSelected` trait.

Solo and split geometry are identical (6pt outer gutter + 4pt inset), which
made the `compact` parameter permanently true, so it is deleted across four
files. The card's accent tint goes neutral when the window isn't key.

Run is now per-target: `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)` carries the state machine
and the selection-scoped overload delegates to it. `isEditingTextField` stays on
the selection door only, which also fixes a latent bug — a Run *click* while the
sidebar filter held focus used to no-op, because that guard was written for
ambient ⌘R. The button is shown even with no run command configured; pressing it
opens Project Settings with the warning, the same branch ⌘R has used since #127.

Notable fixes found while building it:

- `GestureMask.none` would have shipped dead buttons. The header carries the
  group-drag gesture, and `.none` disables every gesture in the SUBVIEW
  hierarchy as well as the added one — solo, that kills the header's own Run and
  Open-in. Hover is `.onHover`, not a gesture, so they would have looked alive.
  `.subviews` drops only the drag.
- A solo missing-directory workroom never reached `WorkroomSplitView` at all
  (`RootView` had its own `isMissing` branch), so "always" was false for it.
  `TargetTerminalDetail` now owns that state for every pane as a ZStack sibling,
  not a structural branch under a live surface.
- The "Open in…" icon ignored its own `.frame`: it was a hidden SF Symbol with
  the icon in an `.overlay`, and an overlay takes its base's size, so the icon
  rendered at whatever the ambient font made the symbol. It is sized directly now.
- `ExternalEditor.installed` was an uncached computed property doing three
  LaunchServices lookups per evaluation, about to run once per visible pane;
  `icon` mutated the size of an image `NSWorkspace` may share. Both cached, and
  the icon is drawn into a fresh image.
- Divider-drag ratios are held in local `@State` and committed on mouse-up
  instead of publishing to the store per mouse-moved tick, which rebuilt every
  pane at cursor rate.
- Chip-drop hit-testing planned against the unpadded detail rect while the
  renderer plans inside the gutter, so a drop in the gutter split with no preview.

`SplitPaneUITests` asserted a collapsed split leaves ZERO title bars; it now
leaves one, and the ✕ is what distinguishes collapsed from still-split.
`TabReorderMathTests`' compact-inset case no longer describes a distinction the
app makes, so it is restated as plain arithmetic.

---
name: macapp-xcuitest-automation-wedge
description: XCUITest "Timed out while enabling automation mode" is a transient environment wedge, not a code failure — confirm with an untouched test, and retry later before resorting to a login-session reset.
metadata:
  type: project
---

macapp XCUITest runs can fail with `The test runner failed to initialize for UI testing.
(Underlying Error: Timed out while enabling automation mode.)`. This is the **automation
subsystem**, not the code: `make app-build` and `make app-test` (unit) keep passing, because they
never enter UI-testing automation mode.

**Diagnose it in one run:** re-run a test that your change did NOT touch (e.g.
`WorkroomAppUITests/WorkroomsViewUITests/testActiveWorkroomShowsATab`). Same error on an untouched
test ⇒ environment, so don't debug your diff.

**It can clear on its own.** Observed 2026-07-31: wedged for a stretch of a session, then every
XCUITest ran green later in the same session with no login-out, no reboot, nothing but elapsed
time and intervening builds. So **retry before escalating** — a login-session reset is the last
resort, not the first response. (An earlier version of this note said a reset was required; that
overstated it.)

Related: [[macapp-uitest-only-relevant-class]] for how to scope runs (`make app-uitest` ignores
`APP_TEST_FLAGS` — call `xcodebuild` with `-only-testing:<Class>[/<method>]`), and
[[macapp-xcuitest-gotchas]] for what is and isn't queryable.

Reading results: `** TEST SUCCEEDED **` alone is not proof anything ran — a run with zero tests
also succeeds, and an `XCTSkip` counts as neither pass nor fail. Get per-test verdicts from the
`.xcresult`:
`xcrun xcresulttool get test-results tests --path <…>.xcresult` and check each `Test Case` node's
`result`.

---
name: verify-macapp-tests
description: "How to read pass/fail from `make app-test` on this repo's macOS app under Xcode 26"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 1236ba7d-24d3-4675-a4db-1d52ca8c5d65
---

`make app-test` (xcodebuild test) on the macapp emits very long verbose lines under Xcode 26 /
macOS 26.5 SDK and does NOT print a "Test Suite … passed" summary to stdout — grepping the log for
it finds nothing even on success. To confirm results, trust the `make` exit code AND/OR query the
result bundle:

```
cd macapp
RESULT=$(find DerivedData -name "*.xcresult" -maxdepth 6 | head -1)
xcrun xcresulttool get test-results summary --path "$RESULT"
```

That prints JSON with `passedTests` / `failedTests` / `result: "Passed"`.

Also: `make app-generate` and `xcodebuild` need the command sandbox disabled — xcodegen/xcodebuild
write to the system temp dir, which the sandbox blocks ("Operation not permitted").

That prints JSON with `passedTests` / `failedTests` / `result: "Passed"`.

**`skippedTests` is the trap.** A `result: "Passed"` run with `failedTests: 0` can still be hiding a

`make app-test` (xcodebuild test) on the macapp emits very long verbose lines under Xcode 26 /
macOS 26.5 SDK and does NOT print a "Test Suite … passed" summary to stdout — grepping the log for

result bundle:

```
cd macapp
RESULT=$(find DerivedData -name "*.xcresult" -maxdepth 6 | head -1)
xcrun xcresulttool get test-results summary --path "$RESULT"
```

That prints JSON with `passedTests` / `failedTests` / `result: "Passed"`.

write to the system temp dir, which the sandbox blocks ("Operation not permitted").

Done. `67748d8d` on master, working tree clean, not pushed.

## The UI tests run now

The automation wedge cleared on its own — proved it was environmental by re-running a test my change didn't touch, which failed identically.

**58 XCUITests, all passing:** pane header (7), split panes + run settings (14), tab-strip overflow (9), and run status / workflow / tab actions / scroll-into-view / window drag / workrooms view (28). Plus 1374 unit.

## Two things the run caught that I'd have shipped

**1. A skip that was silently retiring an assertion.** `testSoloOpenInMenuOpens` reported *skipped*, not passed — my `XCTSkip("no editor installed")` guard keyed on `openIn.menu`, and a SwiftUI `Menu` with `.menuStyle(.button)` doesn't surface as `.buttons` in the a11y tree. You obviously have an editor installed. So the guard fired for the wrong reason and quietly disabled the test. Now keyed on `openIn.primary` (a real Button) with a type-agnostic lookup for the menu — genuinely passing.

**2. A latent bug in the shared scroller, which my change is the first to reach.** `testPinnedAddButtonKeepsGutterFromToolbar` failed with a gap of exactly 0.

`OverflowingTabScroller` pins its "+" via `safeAreaInset(edge: .trailing)`, and that `spacing:` sits between the *chips* and the "+" — leaving the "+" flush with the scroller's trailing edge. `TerminalTabStrip`'s outer `HStack(spacing: 0)` then put the toolbar's first button at exactly that x. Measured: both at 1123.

That's symptom 1 of issue #129, "no abutting". It hid because at the old strip width the fixture's tabs still fit *inline*, where the gap was leftover slack. The new card geometry narrows the strip by 20pt, which pins them. The gutter is explicit now.

I got there by elimination, not inspection: reverting `leadingInset` 4→8 didn't fix it, so I instrumented the assertion with real frames rather than keep theorising.

Amended rather than adding a commit — the original message asserted the UI tests were UNRUN, which would have been a false record. Also corrected two memories: the wedge note gained a second data point (check an untouched test first), and the test-reading note now warns that `skippedTests` can hide a retired assertion behind a green run.

Still outstanding, unchanged: the real-mouse pass. Hover and click on this bar are a known real-mouse-only bug class — synthetic events pass on code a real mouse breaks, so those 58 greens don't settle it.

Concretely: only the things synthetic events can't judge. Everything else is now covered by the 58 XCUITests.

**Launch the fixture** (temp projects, leaves your real config alone):

```bash
open -n "macapp/DerivedData/Build/Products/Debug/Workroom Dev.app" \
  --args -WorkroomUITestFixture 1 -ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES
```

## A. Real mouse only — these are known bug classes here

XCUITest can't drive `.onHover` at all, and synthetic clicks have passed on real-mouse-broken code in this repo before.

1. **Hover each header button** — editor icon, chevron, run, ✕. Each must light its own well. Hover was silently lost once before when the detail's `NavigationSplitView` was dropped; these buttons are new to this location.
2. **Watch the glyph while hovering in/out** — it must not slide or re-settle by a pixel (the `.animation`-scoped-to-fill bug, release/fractional-scale only).
3. **Click each button with a real mouse** — the `.textSelection` class of bug where real `mouseDown` gets eaten but synthetic clicks pass.
4. **Click a non-focused split member's header background** (not a button) — must focus that pane.
5. **Drag a divider** — the ratio is now local state until mouse-up; feel for jank.
6. **Drag a workroom chip into the pane** — the drop preview must appear *before* the split, including a drop inside the new 6pt gutter (that was an off-by-6 I fixed blind).
7. **Grab the header at ~70% width and drag the group** — it must move, and no button may fire.

## B. Your eye — several are numbers you just picked

8. App icon at 18pt against the 13pt symbols. The one you tuned; this is the confirm.
9. The **~4.5pt glyph-centre offset** between the header toolbar and the tab toolbar below it. Inherent to keeping both button styles — hit-target edges align, glyph centres can't.
10. The **reserved gap left of Run** when idle (space held for Restart).
11. The new divider's weight and placement.
12. **Accent tint on a light theme** — `accent @ 0.10` has no guaranteed contrast.
13. **Deactivate the window** — tint must go neutral.
14. Unfocused split member at 0.45 opacity — recedes without looking disabled.
15. Card geometry: 6+4, card edge 8pt off the sidebar card.
16. **Narrow a 3-way split** — label caps at 180pt, and the ✕ must never be the thing squeezed out.

## C. Two states the fixture can't reach

17. **Missing directory** — delete a member's directory *after* the group forms (`insertWorkroomSplit` refuses an already-missing workroom), and separately delete a solo workroom's directory. Both should show the header + warning triangle, no Open-in.
18. **Same workroom in two windows** — one shows Run, the other Stop. Pre-existing and unchanged, but now two headers make it visible. Pressing Run on the non-owner should focus the owning window, not fork a second server.

The ones I'd not skip: **1, 3, 8, 13**. 1 and 3 are the classes that have actually bitten this codebase; 8 is the change you asked for twice and I got wrong twice; 13 is the one accessibility concession I made on your behalf.
